question: The marked price of an article is ₹4,500. It is sold at successive discounts of 25% and 20%. Find the selling price of the article (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective single discount = 25% + 20% − (25 × 20) ÷ 100 = 45% − 5% = 40%

Selling Price (SP) = (100% − 40%) of Marked Price

SP = 60% of ₹4,500 = (60 ÷ 100) × 4500

SP = 60 × 45 = ₹2,700

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹4,500

First discount (D₁) = 25%

Second discount (D₂) = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − D₁ ÷ 100) × (1 − D₂ ÷ 100)

 
 
 

 
 
 Successive Discounts Calculation
 
 
 MP: ₹4500
 
 
• 
 −25%
 
 
 ₹3375
 
 
• 
 −20%
 
 
 SP: ₹2700

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 4500 × (1 − 25 ÷ 100) × (1 − 20 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 4500 × (75 ÷ 100) × (80 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 4500 × (3 ÷ 4) × (4 ÷ 5)

⇒ SP = 4500 × (12 ÷ 20)

⇒ SP = 4500 × (3 ÷ 5)

⇒ SP = 900 × 3

⇒ SP = 2700

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Successive Discount

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula: [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price (MP) vs Cost Price (CP)

Discount is strictly calculated on the Marked Price (also known as Tag Price), whereas Profit or Loss is strictly calculated on the Cost Price.

Multiplier Strategy

To rapidly apply a decrease of R%, directly multiply the base value by the fraction (100 − R) ÷ 100. This method stacks multiplicatively for any number of successive changes.
